satellites.why_cited: The reference MCP server for Snowflake — Cortex AI, object management, SQL orchestration, semantic views. This is what an agent CALLS once a person knows what to ask it for.
satellites.not_good_at: Knows nothing about learning. It can run a query; it cannot tell you which of 58 courses teaches you to write that query.

satellites.why_cited: The most-starred agentic layer over Cortex Code — structured multi-agent workflows for data-engineering projects. The closest thing to a "Snowflake agent OS" that exists, and the reason snowflake-os defines itself by layer.
satellites.not_good_at: Operates on a project, not on a person. No notion of competency, sequence, effort or evidence of learning.

satellites.why_cited: A framework plus agent skills for assessing whether data is AI-ready. The closest sibling in spirit to our gates — it scores a thing rather than asserting it.
satellites.not_good_at: Scores the DATA's readiness, never the engineer's.

satellites.why_cited: Routes Snowflake operations from Claude Code / Cursor / Codex into the Cortex Code CLI. The clearest prior art for "one skill, many runtimes", which is the same shape FDE-os uses.
satellites.not_good_at: Routing, not teaching. And its licence is unresolved — see caution.

satellites.why_cited: Cortex Code plugin with envelope-based permission policy — a real, shipped example of gating what an agent is allowed to do inside a Snowflake account.
satellites.not_good_at: Permissions for an agent, not competency for a human.

satellites.why_cited: Snowflake's own curated Agent Skills for Cortex Code (check-agent-access, dcr-v1-to-v2, manage-zerocopy-sapbdc, mlops) — the nearest published analogue to the skills snowflake-os ships.
satellites.not_good_at: Warehouse operations only; no curriculum surface.

managed_services.name: Snowflake-managed MCP server
managed_services.note: Hosted MCP endpoint exposing Cortex Analyst / Search / Agents, capped at 50 tools per server. Nothing to install. Referenced, not measured — snowflake-os has no Snowflake account under test, so any claim about its behaviour here would be repetition, not verification.
